About

A research engineer working across people, agents, and physical systems

I am a Ph.D. candidate in Civil & Environmental Engineering at Lehigh University, advised within the Complex Adaptive Water Systems Lab. My work combines computational social science, agent-based modeling, LLM evaluation, and research software engineering.

I began with empirical human behavior and human–water systems: survey design, psychometrics, and coupled flood-risk simulation. That foundation now informs how I evaluate generated behavior and design constraint-checked agent systems.

I care about evaluation that reveals disagreement, instability, and limits. The goal is not to claim that an agent is a person; it is to make the relationship between evidence, model behavior, and downstream consequences inspectable.
